# The microbial world

> *How big are microbes, how are they related to each other and to us, and why are most of them harmless?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This unit is planned but not yet written. The outline below shows what it will cover.
:::

## Planned content

- Size and scale, from a red blood cell to a bacterium to a virus
- The tree of life: bacteria, archaea, eukaryotic microbes, and viruses outside the tree
- Most microbes are harmless or useful; pathogens are a small minority
- Prokaryote versus eukaryote, building on cell biology

## Planned interactives

- A zoom across size scales
- Sorting organisms onto the tree of life
- Example: Wolbachia, a bacterium used to stop mosquitoes spreading dengue

**Links to other teaching:** Cell biology.
